# Outline

1. **Which taxa are most dominant** in the vent and non-vent habitat? Consider the class level expression (sum to tax level 4) and occupany pattern (distribution).

2. **For dominant taxa, what is the KEGG BRITE level B composition** in each habitat and taxonomic group?

3. **Define classifications for every KO and taxon** based on occupany/distribution (vent-only, vent-skewed, shared, non-vent-skewed, non-vent-only). The KO table is the hand-off to 06 and 07.

4. **Rarefied sensitivity**: the habitat classes recomputed at equal sequencing depth.


_Definitions_:
**Unit expression.** Below, a unit expression is the scaledTPM that remains after Eukaryota-only assignments and Opisthokonta other than choanoflagellates are removed, averaged over replicates. Every proportion below is taken against that total.

**Detection/prevalence.** A feature is detected in a sample unit when its unit total is ≥ `detect_min_tpm` (1) scaledTPM **and** ≥ `detect_min_per_million` (10) per million of that unit's expression. ScaledTPM carries library size, and unit expression differs about 170-fold among units. A set TPM floor lets deep units detect more. The per-million floor preserves the samples that were sequenced deeply, the TPM floor preserves shallow ones.

**Occupancy/Distribution.** Associated with a habitat = detected in at least 3 units of that habitat (`vent_min_units`, `nonvent_min_units`: >= 3 of 13 vent units, >= 3 of 6 non-vent units). A count rather than a fraction: non-vent has only 6 units, so the bar is "seen in at least three biological units" in both habitats. **Vent-only** = vent-associated and never detected in background water. Plume units are vent-influenced, so a plume detection does not break vent-only (`ventonly_tolerated_tokens`; decision 2026-11-23, was: no non-vent unit at >= 30% occupancy).

**Habitat bins.** Units are binned as vent (13) or non-vent (6: 3 plume, 3 background; `bin_vent()`), and every community test uses this binary. Plume has two roles in the classes: it counts as non-vent for association (>= 3 of the 6 plume + background units), but only a background detection removes a feature from vent-only.

_Methods text_: Samples were binned as vent (13 units) or non-vent (6 units: 3 plume, 3 background). Because plume water is vent-derived, a feature was called vent-only when it was vent-associated and never detected in background water; plume detections were permitted.

**Counts are relative.** A smaller sum of scaltedTPM at vents means a smaller slice of protist expression, not fewer cells.

# Set up

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
source(if (file.exists("_setup.R")) "_setup.R" else "scripts/_setup.R")
```

```{r params}
FIELDS_IN_SCOPE <- c("Gorda Ridge", "Von Damm", "Piccard")
CHOSEN_DEPTH  <- 4 # tax level setting

# Set in params in config/
MIN_TPM <- params$detect_min_tpm; MIN_TPM # 1
MIN_PER_MILLION <- params$detect_min_per_million; MIN_PER_MILLION #10
MIN_UNITS <- c(vent = params$vent_min_units, nonvent = params$nonvent_min_units); MIN_UNITS # 3, 3
VENTONLY_TOLERATED <- params$ventonly_tolerated_tokens; VENTONLY_TOLERATED # "Plume"

# thresholds for taxa across habitats
N_LEADERS <- 10 # top ten taxa per habitat shown
N_RAREFY <- 20 # rarefaction draws
# the 95th-percentile permutation threshold (perm95_threshold) marks it as significant.
DELTA_ENRICH <- 0.5 # |Cliff's delta| >= this = enriched / overrepresented 
```

```{r prep}
# built once at the end of 02 (R/load_paired.R)
paired <- load_paired(fields = FIELDS_IN_SCOPE, depth = CHOSEN_DEPTH)

units <- paired |>
  distinct(unit = sample_unit, vent_bin, field, n_reps) |>
  arrange(vent_bin, field, unit)
# stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(units$unit))
units |> count(vent_bin, field) #Check numebr
```

# Sequencing depth and the detection rule

Subset transcripts based on detection/prevalence rules. Setting TPM floor and the combined rule. The combined rule should track depth much less **within** a habitat.

```{r depth-check}
#| message: true

### Uses a written script, loaded.
ko_unit <- unit_expression(paired, "ko_id", 
                           min_tpm = MIN_TPM,
                           min_per_million = MIN_PER_MILLION)

depth_check <- ko_unit |>
  summarise(unit_total = first(unit_total), #Get first in vector
            ko_tpm_floor = sum(tpm >= MIN_TPM),
            ko_detected = sum(detected),
            .by = c(unit, vent_bin, field)) |>
  arrange(unit_total)

depth_check |> mutate(unit_total = round(unit_total))
# ?cor()
depth_check |>
  summarise(rho_tpm_floor = cor(unit_total, ko_tpm_floor, method = "spearman"),
            rho_combined = cor(unit_total, ko_detected, method = "spearman"),
            median_depth = median(unit_total),
            median_ko_detected = median(ko_detected),
            .by = vent_bin)
```

_Trying to set a detection limit_: the above code sets a rule/threshold for > min_tpm and > min_per_million to reduce within-habitat depth dependence. We have a very different number of vent sites per field, so that is as sampling bias to consider. non-vent samples are too small to assess

# 1. Who leads each habitat

Class level (level 4) taxa summed and `mean_share` is the mean across taxa/metabolism, so every unit counts once regardless of depth. Median and maximum tpm are associated with each, so a mean in by one unit is a single-vent bloom, not a habitat-wide pattern.

```{r leaders}
#| message: true

# Defining major taxa
tax_unit <- unit_expression(paired, c("cur_group", "cur_L4"),
                            min_tpm = MIN_TPM, 
                            min_per_million = MIN_PER_MILLION)

tax_hab <- habitat_occupancy(tax_unit, 
                              units, c("cur_group", "cur_L4"),
                              MIN_UNITS, VENTONLY_TOLERATED) |>
  mutate(taxon = taxon_label_unique(cur_L4), .after = cur_L4)


group_unit <- unit_expression(paired, "cur_group")

group_totals <- complete_units(group_unit, units, "cur_group") |>
  summarise(mean_share = mean(share), 
            median_share = median(share),
            min_share = min(share), 
            max_share = max(share),
            .by = c(cur_group, vent_bin)) |>
  arrange(vent_bin, 
          desc(mean_share))

# taxa needed to reach 50% / 80% of mean expression in each habitat
dominance <- bind_rows(
  tax_hab |> 
    transmute(vent_bin = "Vent", s = mean_share_vent),
  tax_hab |> 
    transmute(vent_bin = "Non-vent", s = mean_share_nonvent)) |>
  arrange(vent_bin, desc(s)) |>
  mutate(cumul = cumsum(s), .by = vent_bin) |>
  summarise(n_taxa_50 = sum(cumul < 0.5) + 1L,
            n_taxa_80 = sum(cumul < 0.8) + 1L,
            n_taxa_detected = sum(s > 0), .by = vent_bin)
dominance

# Get the top NUMBER OF LEADER taxa for vents and non-vents. Defined above (n=10).
leaders <- union(slice_max(tax_hab, mean_share_vent, n = N_LEADERS)$cur_L4,
                 slice_max(tax_hab, mean_share_nonvent, n = N_LEADERS)$cur_L4)

## Which overlap?
intersect(slice_max(tax_hab, mean_share_vent, n = N_LEADERS)$cur_L4,
                 slice_max(tax_hab, mean_share_nonvent, n = N_LEADERS)$cur_L4)

tax_hab |>
  filter(cur_L4 %in% leaders) |>
  left_join(group_totals |>
              select(cur_group, vent_bin, mean_share) |>
              pivot_wider(names_from = vent_bin, values_from = mean_share,
                          names_prefix = "group_"),
            by = "cur_group") |>
  arrange(desc(`group_Vent` + `group_Non-vent`), desc(mean_share_vent + mean_share_nonvent)) |>
  transmute(cur_group,
            group_vent = 100 * `group_Vent`, group_nonvent = 100 * `group_Non-vent`,
            taxon,
            vent_mean = 100 * mean_share_vent, vent_median = 100 * median_share_vent,
            vent_max = 100 * max_share_vent, vent_occ = occ_vent,
            nonvent_mean = 100 * mean_share_nonvent, nonvent_median = 100 * median_share_nonvent,
            nonvent_occ = occ_nonvent, habitat_class) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

> For results: which curated groups and class-level taxa lead each habitat, and which leaders differ between habitats in share versus in occupancy.

## Composition contrast: vent versus non-vent

Shares sum to 1 within a unit, so a larger share for one taxon forces smaller shares elsewhere. The contrast is therefore tested on robust-CLR values (zeros kept at 0, the 02/04 choice), and shares are used only for display. Three outputs:

* **Whole composition:** PERMANOVA on rclr Euclidean (Aitchison) distance, vent versus non-vent, with a PERMDISP check; 13 vs. 6 units is unbalanced, so a dispersion difference can masquerade as a location difference.
* **Per taxon:** Cliff's delta (vent focal) on rclr, with a 95th-percentile permutation threshold across all features in the family, the same primary filter as 05.
* **Display:** each unit's share, zero where absent, with the habitat median.

Units, not libraries, are the replicates throughout.


```{r composition-contrast}
#| message: true
N_PERM_COMP <- 2000

composition_rclr <- function(ue, by_col) {
  ue |>
    select(unit, feature = all_of(by_col), tpm) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |>
    column_to_rownames("unit") |>
    as.matrix() |>
    rclr_transform()
}

compare_composition <- function(z, n_perm = N_PERM_COMP) {
  hab <- set_names(units$vent_bin, units$unit)[rownames(z)]
  observed <- contrast_ranks(z, hab, "Vent")
  null_max <- map_dbl(seq_len(n_perm), \(i)
    max(abs(contrast_ranks(z, set_names(sample(hab), names(hab)), "Vent")), na.rm = TRUE))
  tibble(feature = names(observed), cliffs_delta = observed,
         # >SKH: 2026-11-12 50th and 75th percentiles added for the 1-2-3 asterisk tiers (Figure 3)
         perm50_threshold = unname(quantile(null_max, 0.50)),
         perm75_threshold = unname(quantile(null_max, 0.75)),
         perm95_threshold = unname(quantile(null_max, 0.95))) |>
    # enriched: effect-size line; significant: beyond the 95th percentile of the permuted largest |delta|
    mutate(enriched    = abs(cliffs_delta) >= DELTA_ENRICH,
           significant = abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm95_threshold)
}

set.seed(params$seed)
z_group <- composition_rclr(group_unit, "cur_group")
z_taxon <- composition_rclr(tax_unit, "cur_L4")

# whole composition: PERMANOVA + PERMDISP on rclr Euclidean distance
composition_permanova <- imap_dfr(list(curated_group = z_group, class_level = z_taxon), \(z, grain) {
  meta <- tibble(unit = rownames(z)) |> left_join(units, by = "unit")
  d <- vegan::vegdist(z, method = "euclidean")
  perm <- vegan::adonis2(d ~ vent_bin, data = meta, permutations = 9999)
  disp <- vegan::permutest(vegan::betadisper(d, meta$vent_bin), permutations = 9999)
  tibble(grain, n_features = ncol(z), R2 = perm$R2[1], p = perm$`Pr(>F)`[1],
         dispersion_p = disp$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1])
})
composition_permanova

composition_group <- compare_composition(z_group) |>
  rename(cur_group = feature) |>
  left_join(group_totals |>
              select(cur_group, vent_bin, mean_share, median_share) |>
              pivot_wider(names_from = vent_bin, values_from = c(mean_share, median_share)),
            by = "cur_group") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(cliffs_delta)))

composition_taxon <- compare_composition(z_taxon) |>
  rename(cur_L4 = feature) |>
  left_join(tax_hab |> select(cur_group, cur_L4, taxon, mean_share_vent, mean_share_nonvent,
                              occ_vent, occ_nonvent),
            by = "cur_L4") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(cliffs_delta)))

composition_group |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
composition_taxon |> filter(cur_L4 %in% leaders) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```
```{r fig-delta-distribution}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false

perm95_line <- unique(composition_taxon$perm95_threshold)

stopifnot(length(perm95_line) == 1, DELTA_ENRICH > 0, DELTA_ENRICH < perm95_line)

delta_bands <- c("Below enrichment line", "Enriched", "Significant")

delta_dist <- composition_taxon |>
  mutate(is_leader = cur_L4 %in% leaders,
         band = case_when(abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm95_line   ~ "Significant",
                          abs(cliffs_delta) >= DELTA_ENRICH  ~ "Enriched",
                          TRUE                               ~ "Below enrichment line"),
         band = factor(band, levels = delta_bands))

# what each line would put in the results, and which habitat it leans to
delta_dist |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            higher_at_vent    = sum(cliffs_delta > 0),
            higher_at_nonvent = sum(cliffs_delta < 0),
            n_leaders         = sum(is_leader),
            .by = band) |>
  arrange(band)

# one row per drawn line: both tails of both thresholds
delta_guides <- tibble(
    kind = rep(c("95th-percentile permutation threshold", "Enrichment line"), each = 2),
    x    = c(perm95_line, -perm95_line, DELTA_ENRICH, -DELTA_ENRICH)) |>
  mutate(kind = fct_inorder(kind))

fig_delta_dist <- ggplot(delta_dist, aes(x = cliffs_delta)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = band), binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0,
                 colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_rug(data = \(d) filter(d, is_leader), sides = "b",
           colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(data = delta_guides, aes(xintercept = x, linetype = kind),
             colour = "grey15", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Below enrichment line" = "grey82",
                               "Enriched"              = "#E69F00",
                               "Significant"           = "#0072B2"),
                    breaks = rev(delta_bands), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("95th-percentile permutation threshold" = "solid",
                                   "Enrichment line"                       = "22"),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.05, 1.05)) +
  labs(x = "Cliff's delta on rCLR (vent focal; positive = higher at vents)",
       y = "Class-level taxa") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.direction = "vertical")

fig_delta_dist
# ggsave("figures/05-delta-distribution.svg", fig_delta_dist, width = 7, height = 4)
```
> Distribution of Cliff's delta on robust CLR values across every class-level taxon, positive means higher rank in vents. Solid lines mark the 95th-percentile permutation threshold: the 95th percentile of the largest |delta| across all taxa when habitat labels are shuffled across units (a family-wise null). Dashed lines mark the enrichment line at |delta| = `DELTA_ENRICH`, a chosen effect-size cutoff, not a test. Ticks along the lower axis mark the leading taxa. Based on 13 vent and 6 non-vent units

> For results: how many taxa are enriched (|delta| >= `DELTA_ENRICH`) versus significant (beyond the 95th-percentile permutation threshold), and which habitat they lean to. Only the permutation threshold is calibrated against the shuffled-label null; `DELTA_ENRICH` is an effect-size convention and must be named as one.

## Figure: every taxon on robust-CLR

Geometric mean (rCLR) for all taxa


```{r fig-taxa-heatmap}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 18
#| warning: false
#| 
# taxa kept: pass the occupancy filter in at least one habitat
heat_taxa <- tax_hab |>
  filter(habitat_class != "below_filter") |>
  select(cur_group, cur_L4, taxon) |>
  left_join(composition_taxon |> select(cur_L4, cliffs_delta, perm95_threshold),
            by = "cur_L4") |>
  mutate(significant = abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm95_threshold,
         row_lab     = if_else(significant, paste0(taxon, " *"), taxon),
         cur_group  = factor(cur_group,
                             levels = intersect(SUPERGROUP_0_ordering, unique(cur_group)))) |>
  arrange(cur_group, desc(cliffs_delta)) |>
  mutate(row_lab = fct_rev(fct_inorder(row_lab)))

# units x taxa rCLR to long; rclr_transform() leaves absent taxa at exactly 0
heat_long <- z_taxon |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "unit") |>
  pivot_longer(-unit, names_to = "cur_L4", values_to = "rclr") |>
  inner_join(heat_taxa, by = "cur_L4") |>
  left_join(units |> select(unit, vent_bin), by = "unit") |>
  mutate(rclr     = na_if(rclr, 0),
         vent_bin = fct_relevel(factor(vent_bin), "Vent"),
         unit_lab = factor(unit, levels = order_sample_names, labels = label_sample_names))

# stopifnot(!anyNA(heat_long$unit_lab), !anyNA(heat_long$vent_bin))

rclr_cap <- quantile(abs(heat_long$rclr), 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

fig_taxa_heatmap <- ggplot(heat_long, aes(x = unit_lab, y = row_lab, fill = rclr)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = -1,
                       limits = c(-rclr_cap, rclr_cap), oob = scales::squish,
                       na.value = "grey88", name = "rCLR") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = "right") +
  facet_grid(cur_group ~ vent_bin, scales = "free", space = "free", switch = "y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, color = "black"),
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        panel.spacing = grid::unit(2, "pt"),
        legend.position = "top")

fig_taxa_heatmap

# ggsave("figures/05-taxa-heatmap.svg", fig_taxa_heatmap, width = 5, height = 18)
```

> For results: whether the significant taxa are carried by consistent shifts across units or by presence/absence in a few units, and which curated groups hold them.

# 2. Taxonomic group functional signatures (KEGG level B)

Each KO is placed in its KEGG level-B categories (`read_brite_level_b()`, the same map as 04 and 06); a KO in *n* categories splits its TPM equally across them. Shares are of **mapped** expression only; the coverage table says how much that is per unit.

```{r kegg-habitat}
#| message: true
brite_map <- read_brite_level_b()

kegg_long <- paired |>
  select(sample_unit, n_reps, vent_bin, field, cur_group, cur_L4, ko_id, scaledTPM) |>
  inner_join(brite_map |> select(ko_id, a_description, description, n_cat),
             by = "ko_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cat)

kegg_coverage <- unit_expression(paired |> 
                                   mutate(mapped = ko_id %in% brite_map$ko_id), "mapped") |>
  filter(mapped) |>
  select(unit, vent_bin, mapped_share = share)

kegg_coverage |> summarise(min = min(mapped_share), median = median(mapped_share),
                           max = max(mapped_share), .by = vent_bin)

kegg_unit <- unit_expression(kegg_long, c("a_description", "description"))

kegg_by_habitat <- complete_units(kegg_unit, units, c("a_description", "description")) |>
  summarise(mean_share = mean(share), median_share = median(share),
            .by = c(a_description, description, vent_bin)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = vent_bin, values_from = c(mean_share, median_share)) |>
  arrange(desc(`mean_share_Vent` + `mean_share_Non-vent`))

kegg_by_habitat |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(100 * x, 2)))
```

Per-taxon profiles: for each leading taxon, its expression split across level-B
categories within each unit where it is detected, averaged over those units.

```{r kegg-leaders}
#| message: true
taxon_kegg_unit <- unit_expression(kegg_long |> filter(cur_L4 %in% leaders),
                                   c("cur_group", "cur_L4", "description")) |>
  mutate(taxon_share = tpm / sum(tpm), .by = c(unit, cur_L4))

detected_taxa <- tax_unit |> filter(detected) |> distinct(unit, cur_L4)

leader_kegg <- taxon_kegg_unit |>
  semi_join(detected_taxa, by = c("unit", "cur_L4")) |>
  select(unit, vent_bin, cur_group, cur_L4, description, taxon_share) |>
  complete(nesting(unit, vent_bin, cur_group, cur_L4), description,
           fill = list(taxon_share = 0)) |>
  summarise(mean_taxon_share = mean(taxon_share), n_units = n_distinct(unit),
            .by = c(vent_bin, cur_group, cur_L4, description)) |>
  mutate(taxon = taxon_label_unique(cur_L4))

leader_kegg |> filter(mean_taxon_share >= 0.05) |>
  arrange(cur_L4, vent_bin, desc(mean_taxon_share)) |>
  mutate(mean_taxon_share = round(100 * mean_taxon_share, 1))
```

## Alternative view: paired dots, vent vs. non-vent

Same data as the heatmap above, drawn so the habitat contrast is the picture. Each panel is
one leading taxon. For each KEGG level-B category, the line joins the taxon's mean share of
its own mapped expression in non-vent units to its share in vent units. A long line marks a
category where **the same lineage** expresses a different mix in the two habitats. A taxon
is drawn only if it was detected in at least 2 units in each habitat.

## Figures: KEGG level B on robust-CLR

Same idea as the taxa heatmap, for function. rCLR is computed once over **all** level-B categories (21 after the excluded A blocks and the level-B curation), and the top-20 figures show a subset of those same values, so the color of a cell is identical in both versions. Grey is absent, not 0.

* **Community:** each unit's mapped expression across level-B categories, with Cliff's delta (vent focal) and the 95th-percentile permutation threshold over all categories.
* **Within taxon:** for every occupancy-filtered taxon, the rCLR of its own level-B mix in each unit where it is detected, averaged over those units per habitat. The reference is the geometric mean of the categories that taxon expresses in that unit, so taxa with little mapped expression (few categories) are noisier.

```{r kegg-rclr}
#| message: true
# level-B order: grouped by level A
cat_order <- kegg_by_habitat |>
  distinct(a_description, description) |>
  arrange(a_description, description)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(cat_order$description))

# community: units x categories rCLR, contrast over all categories
set.seed(params$seed)
z_kegg <- composition_rclr(kegg_unit, "description")
composition_kegg <- compare_composition(z_kegg) |>
  rename(description = feature) |>
  mutate(significant = abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm95_threshold,
         # >SKH: 2026-11-12 asterisk tiers on the permuted largest |delta|:
         # * >= 50th, ** >= 75th, *** >= 95th percentile (*** = significant)
         delta_stars = case_when(abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm95_threshold ~ "***",
                                 abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm75_threshold ~ "**",
                                 abs(cliffs_delta) >= perm50_threshold ~ "*",
                                 TRUE ~ ""))

kegg_heat_long <- z_kegg |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "unit") |>
  pivot_longer(-unit, names_to = "description", values_to = "rclr") |>
  left_join(cat_order, by = "description") |>
  left_join(composition_kegg, by = "description") |>
  left_join(units |> select(unit, vent_bin), by = "unit") |>
  mutate(rclr  = na_if(rclr, 0),
         vent_bin = fct_relevel(factor(vent_bin), "Vent"),
         unit_lab = factor(unit, levels = order_sample_names, labels = label_sample_names),
         row_lab= if_else(delta_stars != "", paste(description, delta_stars), description)) |>
  arrange(a_description, desc(cliffs_delta)) |>
  mutate(row_lab = fct_rev(fct_inorder(row_lab)))

composition_kegg |>
  left_join(cat_order, by = "description") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(cliffs_delta))) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

# within taxon: rCLR of each taxon's level-B mix, per unit where the taxon is detected
taxon_kegg_rclr <- unit_expression(kegg_long |> filter(cur_L4 %in% heat_taxa$cur_L4),
                                   c("cur_L4", "description")) |>
  semi_join(detected_taxa, by = c("unit", "cur_L4")) |>
  filter(tpm > 0) |>
  mutate(rclr = log(tpm) - mean(log(tpm)), .by = c(unit, cur_L4)) |>
  summarise(mean_rclr = mean(rclr), n_units = n_distinct(unit),
            .by = c(vent_bin, cur_L4, description)) |>
  mutate(vent_bin = as.character(vent_bin))

# every taxon x category x habitat, so never-expressed cells draw as grey
taxon_kegg_long <- heat_taxa |>
  select(cur_group, cur_L4, row_lab) |>
  cross_join(cat_order) |>
  cross_join(tibble(vent_bin = c("Vent", "Non-vent"))) |>
  left_join(taxon_kegg_rclr, by = c("vent_bin", "cur_L4", "description")) |>
  mutate(vent_bin    = factor(vent_bin, levels = c("Vent", "Non-vent")),
         description = factor(description, levels = cat_order$description))

# shared color caps so the all-category and top-20 versions match
kegg_cap  <- quantile(abs(kegg_heat_long$rclr), 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
taxon_cap <- quantile(abs(taxon_kegg_long$mean_rclr), 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

rclr_fill <- function(cap) {
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = -1,
                       limits = c(-cap, cap), oob = scales::squish,
                       na.value = "grey88", name = "rCLR")
}

heat_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        panel.spacing= grid::unit(2, "pt"),
        legend.position = "top")

plot_kegg_units <- function(df) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = unit_lab, y = row_lab, fill = rclr)) +
    geom_tile(color = "grey5", linewidth = 0.3) +
    rclr_fill(kegg_cap) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = "right") +
    facet_grid(a_description ~ vent_bin, scales = "free", space = "free", switch = "y",
               labeller = labeller(a_description = label_wrap_gen(18))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    heat_theme +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0))
}

plot_taxon_kegg <- function(df) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = description, y = row_lab, fill = mean_rclr)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "grey15", linewidth = 0.3) +
    rclr_fill(taxon_cap) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = "right") +
    facet_grid(cur_group ~ vent_bin, scales = "free", space = "free", switch = "y") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    heat_theme +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, color = "black"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0))
}
```

## Alternative view: same lineage or different lineages?

For each KEGG level-B category, the vent minus non-vent difference in its share of mapped
expression is split into two parts (a midpoint shift-share decomposition, summed over
class-level taxa):

* **Same lineage, different expression:** each lineage expresses the category at a different
  share of its own expression in the two habitats.
* **Different lineages lead:** the lineages that carry the expression differ between habitats,
  so the category changes even if each lineage behaved the same.

The two parts add exactly to the difference, and the total is checked against
`kegg_by_habitat`. Lineages absent from one habitat contribute only to the second part.

```{r kegg-shift-decomposition}
#| message: true
# lineage grain for the decomposition: "cur_L4" (class-level taxa) or "cur_group" (supergroups)
lineage_col <- "cur_L4"

n_hab <- count(units, vent_bin, name = "n_units")

# mean over ALL units of a habitat (absent = 0) of each lineage x category share of mapped expression
shift_mass <- unit_expression(kegg_long, c(lineage_col, "description")) |>
  select(unit, vent_bin, lineage = all_of(lineage_col), description, share) |>
  summarise(mass = sum(share), .by = c(vent_bin, lineage, description)) |>
  left_join(n_hab, by = "vent_bin") |>
  mutate(mass = mass / n_units) |>
  select(-n_units)

shift_wide <- shift_mass |>
  complete(vent_bin, lineage, description, fill = list(mass = 0)) |>
  mutate(w = sum(mass), .by = c(vent_bin, lineage)) |>                 # lineage share of mapped expression
  mutate(p = if_else(w > 0, mass / w, NA_real_)) |>                     # category profile within lineage
  pivot_wider(names_from = vent_bin, values_from = c(w, p, mass)) |>
  mutate(p_vent    = coalesce(p_Vent, `p_Non-vent`),                    # absent habitat: borrow the other profile
         p_nonvent = coalesce(`p_Non-vent`, p_Vent),
         within      = (w_Vent + `w_Non-vent`) / 2 * (p_vent - p_nonvent),
         composition = (w_Vent - `w_Non-vent`) * (p_vent + p_nonvent) / 2,
         delta       = mass_Vent - `mass_Non-vent`)

shift_decomp <- shift_wide |>
  summarise(within_lineage = sum(within), composition = sum(composition), delta = sum(delta),
            .by = description)

# the two parts must add to the difference, and the difference must match kegg_by_habitat
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(shift_decomp$within_lineage + shift_decomp$composition, shift_decomp$delta)))
shift_check <- shift_decomp |>
  left_join(transmute(kegg_by_habitat, description, ref = mean_share_Vent - `mean_share_Non-vent`),
            by = "description")
stopifnot(max(abs(shift_check$delta - shift_check$ref)) < 1e-8)

shift_decomp |>
  arrange(desc(abs(delta))) |>
  mutate(across(c(within_lineage, composition, delta), \(x) round(100 * x, 2)))
```

```{r fig-kegg-shift}
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 6
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Shift-share decomposition of the vent minus non-vent difference in each KEGG level-B category's proportion of mapped expression (percentage points), summed over class-level taxa. Horizontal axis: the part contributed by which lineages carry the expression. Vertical axis: the part contributed by the same lineage expressing the category at a different proportion of its own expression. The two parts sum to the total difference, so the falling grey diagonal is where that total is zero; categories above it are higher at vents and categories below it are higher at non-vent sites. The rising grey diagonal marks equal contribution from the two parts. Point area is the absolute total difference and fill names the larger of the two parts. Categories reaching 1 percentage point are labelled, with overlapping labels dropped. Based on 13 vent and 6 non-vent units; the split depends on the lineage grain (`lineage_col`) and is descriptive."

# label categories whose absolute total difference reaches this many percentage points
LABEL_MIN_PP <- 1.0

shift_xy <- shift_decomp |>
  mutate(within_pp = 100 * within_lineage,
         comp_pp = 100 * composition,
         delta_pp = 100 * delta,
         larger_part = if_else(abs(within_lineage) >= abs(composition),
                               "Same lineage, different expression",
                               "Different lineages lead"))

fig_kegg_shift <- ggplot(shift_xy, aes(x = comp_pp, y = within_pp)) +
  # delta = within_lineage + composition, so the falling line is total difference = 0
  # and the rising line is where the two parts contribute equally
  geom_abline(slope = c(-1, 1), intercept = 0, colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = larger_part, size = abs(delta_pp)),
             shape = 21, colour = "grey20", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = \(d) d |> filter(abs(delta_pp) >= LABEL_MIN_PP) |>
                        arrange(desc(abs(delta_pp))),
            aes(label = description, hjust = if_else(comp_pp >= 0, -0.12, 1.12)),
            size = 2.5, colour = "grey15", check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Same lineage, different expression" = "#0072B2",
                               "Different lineages lead"            = "#E69F00"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, name = "|Total difference| (pp)") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.10)) +
  labs(x = "Different lineages lead (percentage points)",
       y = "Same lineage, different expression (percentage points)") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3.5))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.direction = "vertical")
# the diagonals sit at the right place on any aspect ratio, but only look like
# 45 degrees under coord_fixed(); add it to judge dominance by eye instead of by fill
fig_kegg_shift
# ggsave("figures/05-kegg-shift.svg", fig_kegg_shift, width = 7.5, height = 6)
```

> For results: the falling diagonal splits vent-higher (above) from non-vent-higher (below); fill says whether the difference came from the same lineages expressing differently or from different lineages leading, and point area gives its size. The split depends on the lineage grain (`lineage_col`) and is descriptive, with 6 non-vent units.

# 3. Habitat classes for KOs and taxa

```{r habitat-classes}
#| message: true
ko_hab <- habitat_occupancy(ko_unit, units, "ko_id", MIN_UNITS, VENTONLY_TOLERATED)

bind_rows(ko_hab |> count(habitat_class) |> mutate(feature = "KO"),
          tax_hab |> count(habitat_class) |> mutate(feature = "class-level taxon")) |>
  mutate(frac = round(n / sum(n), 3), .by = feature) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = c(n, frac), values_fill = 0)

tax_hab |> filter(habitat_class %in% c("vent_only", "nonvent_only")) |>
  select(habitat_class, cur_group, taxon, n_det_vent, n_det_nonvent,
         mean_share_vent, mean_share_nonvent) |>
  arrange(habitat_class, desc(mean_share_vent + mean_share_nonvent))
```

KEGG level-B composition of each KO habitat class (a KO in *n* categories counts 1/*n* in
each; % of mapped KOs in the class).

```{r habitat-class-kegg}
class_levels <- c("vent_only", "vent_skewed", "shared", "nonvent_skewed", "nonvent_only")

ko_class_kegg <- ko_hab |>
  filter(habitat_class %in% class_levels) |>
  transmute(ko_id, habitat_class = as.character(habitat_class)) |>
  left_join(brite_map |> select(ko_id, a_description, description, n_cat),
            by = "ko_id", relationship = "one-to-many")

class_coverage <- ko_class_kegg |>
  summarise(n_ko = n_distinct(ko_id), n_mapped = n_distinct(ko_id[!is.na(description)]),
            .by = habitat_class)

class_kegg <- ko_class_kegg |>
  filter(!is.na(description)) |>
  summarise(ko_weight = sum(1 / n_cat), .by = c(habitat_class, a_description, description)) |>
  complete(habitat_class, nesting(a_description, description), fill = list(ko_weight = 0)) |>
  left_join(class_coverage, by = "habitat_class") |>
  mutate(pct_of_mapped = 100 * ko_weight / n_mapped)

class_coverage
```

```{r fig-class-kegg}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "KEGG level-B composition of each KO habitat class. Columns are habitat classes (n, KOs in the class; mapped, KOs with a level-B assignment). Fill and printed values give the percent of the class's mapped KOs in each category (values below 1% are not printed); a KO in several categories counts 1/n in each. A habitat is associated with a KO when the KO is detected in at least 3 of its units. Vent-only KOs are vent-associated and never detected in background water (plume detections allowed). Rows are grouped by KEGG level-A class."
class_lab <- class_coverage |>
  mutate(lab = glue("{str_replace(habitat_class, '_', '-')}\nn = {n_ko}\n({n_mapped} mapped)")) |>
  select(habitat_class, lab) |> deframe()

fig_class_kegg <- class_kegg |>
  mutate(habitat_class = factor(habitat_class, levels = class_levels),
         description = fct_reorder(description, ko_weight, .fun = sum),
         a_description = str_wrap(a_description, 14)) |>
  ggplot(aes(habitat_class, description, fill = pct_of_mapped)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(pct_of_mapped >= 1, sprintf("%.0f", pct_of_mapped), "")),
            size = 3, colour = "grey5") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#eedac3", high = "#711518",
                      name = "% of mapped\nKOs in class") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = class_lab, position = "top") +
  facet_grid(a_description ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey5"),
        axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5,
                                       size = 7, color = "grey5"))
fig_class_kegg
ggsave("figures/05-class-kegg.svg", fig_class_kegg, width = 8, height = 8)
```
KEGG level-B composition of each KO habitat class. Columns are habitat classes (n, KOs in the class; mapped, KOs with a level-B assignment). Fill and printed values give the percent of the class's mapped KOs in each category (values below 1% are not printed); a KO in several categories counts 1/n in each. A habitat is associated with a KO when the KO is detected in at least 3 of its units. Vent-only KOs are vent-associated and never detected in background water (plume detections allowed). Rows are grouped by KEGG level-A class.

## Alternative view: enrichment in vent-associated KOs

The five habitat classes are merged into three groups: **vent-associated** (vent-only +
vent-skewed), **shared**, and **non-vent-associated** (non-vent-only + non-vent-skewed).
For each KEGG level-B category, observed KOs in a group are compared with the number expected
if KOs fell into groups at random (all mapped, detected KOs as the background).

* Fill is log2(observed / expected), with a 0.5 pseudocount. Red = over-represented, blue = under-represented.
* Dot size is the number of KOs in that category and group (no dot = none).
* `*` marks BH q <= 0.05 (Fisher's exact test, one test per category and group, BH across all of them).
* A KO placed in several categories counts once in each, so these are KO counts, not the fractional weights in the heatmap.
* The vent-associated group is small (31 vent-only + 21 vent-skewed KOs, 34 of them mapped to KEGG level B), so the tests have little power and are exploratory.
* The non-vent-associated group largely reflects the deeper sequencing of non-vent units (see section 5), so read it as a contrast, not as habitat biology.

```{r class-kegg-enrichment}
#| message: true
class_group_map <- c(vent_only = "Vent-associated", vent_skewed = "Vent-associated",
                     shared = "Shared",
                     nonvent_skewed = "Non-vent-associated", nonvent_only = "Non-vent-associated")
class_group_levels <- c("Vent-associated", "Shared", "Non-vent-associated")

ko_cat <- ko_class_kegg |>
  filter(!is.na(description)) |>
  mutate(class_group = factor(unname(class_group_map[habitat_class]), levels = class_group_levels)) |>
  distinct(ko_id, class_group, a_description, description)

group_n <- ko_cat |> distinct(ko_id, class_group) |> count(class_group, name = "n_group")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(distinct(ko_cat, ko_id, class_group)$ko_id))   # each KO sits in one group
universe_n <- sum(group_n$n_group)
cat_total  <- count(ko_cat, description, name = "n_cat_total")          # KOs per category, all groups

class_enrich <- ko_cat |>
  count(class_group, a_description, description, name = "k") |>
  complete(class_group, nesting(a_description, description), fill = list(k = 0L)) |>
  left_join(group_n, by = "class_group") |>
  left_join(cat_total, by = "description") |>
  mutate(N = universe_n,
         expected    = n_group * n_cat_total / N,
         log2_enrich = log2((k + 0.5) / (expected + 0.5)),
         p_fisher = purrr::pmap_dbl(list(k, n_group, n_cat_total, N), \(k, n, K, N)
           stats::fisher.test(matrix(c(k, n - k, K - k, N - n - (K - k)), nrow = 2))$p.value),
         q_bh = p.adjust(p_fisher, method = "BH"),
         sig  = q_bh <= 0.05)

group_n
class_enrich |>
  filter(sig) |>
  arrange(class_group, q_bh) |>
  select(class_group, description, k, expected, log2_enrich, p_fisher, q_bh) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

Asterisks mark BH q <= 0.05 (Fisher's exact test, BH across all category and group tests). The background is all mapped, detected KOs; a KO in several categories counts once in each."

## Enrichment three ways, with the taxa behind each category

The over-representation test above uses only KOs that clear the occupancy classes. Two rank-based versions use every mapped KO detected in at least `MIN_UNITS_RANK` units, ranked by Cliff's delta on rCLR (vent focal; the same statistic as the 95th-percentile permutation threshold contrasts and 07):

* **Rank score, unit permutation.** Category score = mean delta of its KOs minus mean delta of all other KOs. The p-value comes from permuting habitat labels across the 19 units, which keeps the correlation among KOs intact; a test that only shuffles KOs ignores that correlation and is anti-conservative (Goeman & Bühlmann 2007; Wu & Smyth 2012). BH across categories.
* **fgsea.** The same ranked list and level-B sets through `fgsea()` (Subramanian et al. 2005). Its p-values come from gene-set permutation, so they share that anti-conservative bias; shown for comparison with 07.
* **Over-representation.** `fig_class_enrich` as above.

Each is paired with the same taxa panel: for every category, the five class-level taxa with the largest contribution to the vent minus non-vent difference in its share of mapped expression (percentage points; mean over all units of a habitat, absent = 0). Contributions over all taxa sum to the category's total difference, marked with a tick. The panel is in expression units; the ORA counts KOs, so the two can disagree.

```{r enrich-taxa-prep}
#| message: true
MIN_UNITS_RANK <- 2      # KO must be detected in at least this many units to be ranked
N_PERM_SET     <- 4999   # unit-label permutations for the rank score
N_TOP_TAXA     <- 5      # taxa shown per category

# --- taxa responsible: contribution to each category's vent - non-vent difference ---
hab_units <- count(units, vent_bin, name = "n_units")

taxon_contrib <- unit_expression(kegg_long, c("cur_group", "cur_L4", "description")) |>
  summarise(mass = sum(share), .by = c(vent_bin, cur_group, cur_L4, description)) |>
  left_join(hab_units, by = "vent_bin") |>
  mutate(mass = 100 * mass / n_units, vent_bin = as.character(vent_bin)) |>
  select(-n_units) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = vent_bin, values_from = mass, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(contrib_pp = Vent - `Non-vent`,
         taxon      = taxon_label_unique(cur_L4))

cat_total_pp <- taxon_contrib |>
  summarise(total_pp = sum(contrib_pp), .by = description)

# taxa contributions must add back to the category difference in kegg_by_habitat
check_total <- kegg_by_habitat |>
  transmute(description, expected_pp = 100 * (mean_share_Vent - `mean_share_Non-vent`)) |>
  inner_join(cat_total_pp, by = "description")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(check_total$expected_pp, check_total$total_pp, tolerance = 1e-6)))

top_contrib <- taxon_contrib |>
  slice_max(abs(contrib_pp), n = N_TOP_TAXA, by = description, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(desc(abs(contrib_pp))), .by = description)

# --- ranked KOs: rCLR over all KOs, then the mapped, detected subset ---
ko_rank_set <- ko_hab |>
  filter(n_det_vent + n_det_nonvent >= MIN_UNITS_RANK) |>
  pull(ko_id) |>
  intersect(brite_map$ko_id)

z_ko   <- composition_rclr(ko_unit, "ko_id")[, ko_rank_set]
hab_ko <- set_names(units$vent_bin, units$unit)[rownames(z_ko)]
is_vent <- hab_ko == "Vent"
n_v <- sum(is_vent)
n_n <- sum(!is_vent)

# Cliff's delta from fixed within-KO ranks: only the labels move under permutation
rank_mat <- apply(z_ko, 2, rank, ties.method = "average")
delta_from_labels <- function(v) {
  u <- colSums(rank_mat[v, , drop = FALSE]) - n_v * (n_v + 1) / 2
  2 * u / (n_v * n_n) - 1
}
ko_delta <- delta_from_labels(is_vent)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(ko_delta),
                           unname(contrast_ranks(z_ko, hab_ko, "Vent")))))  # matches the shared helper

# KO x category membership (a KO counts once in each of its categories)
ko_cat_b <- brite_map |>
  filter(ko_id %in% colnames(z_ko)) |>
  distinct(ko_id, description)
memb <- ko_cat_b |>
  mutate(x = 1) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = ko_id, names_from = description, values_from = x, values_fill = 0) |>
  column_to_rownames("ko_id") |>
  as.matrix()
memb  <- memb[colnames(z_ko), , drop = FALSE]
set_n <- colSums(memb)

message(glue("{ncol(z_ko)} mapped KOs ranked across {ncol(memb)} level-B categories."))
```

```{r enrich-rank-perm}
#| message: true
cat_score <- function(delta) {
  in_sum <- drop(crossprod(memb, delta))
  in_sum / set_n - (sum(delta) - in_sum) / (length(delta) - set_n)
}

set.seed(params$seed)
score_obs  <- cat_score(ko_delta)
score_null <- replicate(N_PERM_SET, cat_score(delta_from_labels(sample(is_vent))))

rank_enrich <- tibble(description = names(score_obs),
                      score       = score_obs,
                      n_ko        = set_n[names(score_obs)],
                      p_perm      = (1 + rowSums(abs(score_null) >= abs(score_obs))) /
                                    (N_PERM_SET + 1)) |>
  mutate(q_bh = p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH"),
         sig  = q_bh <= 0.05) |>
  left_join(cat_order, by = "description")

rank_enrich |>
  arrange(q_bh) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r enrich-fgsea}
#| message: true
set.seed(params$seed)
fgsea_b <- fgsea::fgsea(pathways = split(ko_cat_b$ko_id, ko_cat_b$description),
                        stats    = ko_delta,
                        minSize  = 5,
                        eps      = 0) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(description = pathway, NES, n_ko = size, pval, padj,
            sig = padj <= 0.05) |>
  left_join(cat_order, by = "description")

fgsea_b |>
  arrange(padj) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

```{r enrich-taxa-helpers}
# left panel: one tile column per test, rows grouped by level A
enrich_tile <- function(df, fill_var, fill_name, col_lab) {
  lim <- max(abs(df[[fill_var]]), na.rm = TRUE)
  df |>
    mutate(description   = fct_reorder(description, .data[[fill_var]]),
           a_description = str_wrap(a_description, 14),
           col           = col_lab) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = col, y = description)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = .data[[fill_var]])) +
    geom_text(data = \(d) filter(d, sig), label = "*", size = 5, vjust = 0.75) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0,
                         limits = c(-lim, lim), name = fill_name) +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    facet_grid(a_description ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid        = element_blank(),
          strip.placement   = "outside",
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 1),
          axis.text.x.top   = element_text(size = 7))
}

# right panel: top taxa per category, signed contribution, aligned to the left panel's rows
taxa_panel <- function(cat_levels) {
  facet_a <- cat_order |> mutate(a_description = str_wrap(a_description, 14))
  bars <- top_contrib |>
    filter(description %in% cat_levels) |>
    left_join(facet_a, by = "description") |>
    mutate(description = factor(description, levels = cat_levels),
           cur_group   = factor(cur_group, levels = SUPERGROUP_0_ordering))
  ticks <- cat_total_pp |>
    filter(description %in% cat_levels) |>
    left_join(facet_a, by = "description") |>
    mutate(description = factor(description, levels = cat_levels))
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.85)

  ggplot(bars, aes(x = contrib_pp, y = description, group = rank)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = cur_group), position = dodge, width = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = taxon, hjust = if_else(contrib_pp >= 0, -0.05, 1.05)),
              position = dodge, size = 1.8, colour = "grey10") +
    geom_point(data = ticks, aes(x = total_pp, y = description), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               shape = 124, size = 4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = tax_color_metaT, name = "Curated group", drop = TRUE) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.4)) +
    facet_grid(a_description ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Contribution to vent − non-vent difference\n(percentage points of mapped expression)",
         y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
          strip.text.y       = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor   = element_blank())
}

with_taxa <- function(p_left, widths = c(1, 3)) {
  p_left + taxa_panel(levels(p_left$data$description)) +
    plot_layout(widths = widths, guides = "collect")
}
```

# Sensitivity: habitat classes at equal depth

Each unit's KO (and taxon) totals, rounded to integer scaledTPM, are rarefied to the
shallowest unit (`vegan::rrarefy`), `N_RAREFY` times. At equal depth, detected = at least
one read. A feature's rarefied class is its most frequent class across draws. Rarefying
is the standard control for uneven effort when presence/absence is compared
(Schloss 2024, *mSphere* 9:e00354-23).

```{r rarefy}
#| message: true
rarefy_classes <- function(ue, by_col) {
  mat <- ue |>
    select(unit, feature = all_of(by_col), tpm) |>
    mutate(tpm = round(tpm)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |>
    column_to_rownames("unit") |>
    as.matrix()
  depth <- min(rowSums(mat))
  hab   <- units$vent_bin[match(rownames(mat), units$unit)]
  bg    <- hab == "Non-vent" & !ventonly_tolerated(rownames(mat), hab, VENTONLY_TOLERATED)
  draws <- map(seq_len(N_RAREFY), \(i) {
    r <- vegan::rrarefy(mat, depth) > 0
    tibble(feature = colnames(mat),
           n_det_vent = colSums(r[hab == "Vent", , drop = FALSE]),
           n_det_nonvent = colSums(r[hab == "Non-vent", , drop = FALSE]),
           n_det_background = colSums(r[bg, , drop = FALSE])) |>
      mutate(class = classify_habitat(n_det_vent, n_det_nonvent, n_det_background,
                                      MIN_UNITS[["vent"]], MIN_UNITS[["nonvent"]]))
  })
  list(depth = depth,
       modal = bind_rows(draws) |>
         count(feature, class) |>
         slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = feature) |>
         transmute(feature, rarefied_class = class, rarefied_agreement = n / N_RAREFY))
}

set.seed(params$seed)
rare_ko  <- rarefy_classes(ko_unit, "ko_id")
rare_tax <- rarefy_classes(tax_unit, "cur_L4")
message(glue("Rarefied to {round(rare_ko$depth)} (KO) / {round(rare_tax$depth)} (taxa) per unit"))

ko_hab <- ko_hab |>
  left_join(rare_ko$modal, by = c("ko_id" = "feature")) |>
  mutate(rarefied_class = factor(coalesce(as.character(rarefied_class), "below_filter"),
                                 levels = levels(habitat_class)))
tax_hab <- tax_hab |>
  left_join(rare_tax$modal, by = c("cur_L4" = "feature")) |>
  mutate(rarefied_class = factor(coalesce(as.character(rarefied_class), "below_filter"),
                                 levels = levels(habitat_class)))

rarefied_agreement <- bind_rows(
  ko_hab |> count(feature = "KO", habitat_class, rarefied_class),
  tax_hab |> count(feature = "class-level taxon", habitat_class, rarefied_class))

rarefied_agreement |>
  summarise(n_features = sum(n), same_class = sum(n[habitat_class == rarefied_class]),
            .by = c(feature, habitat_class)) |>
  mutate(frac_same = round(same_class / n_features, 2))
```

> For results: the share of vent-only and shared KOs that keep their class at equal depth. A vent-only class that does not survive rarefaction rests on depth, not habitat.

# QC

```{r qc}
stopifnot(
  all(unique(paired$field) %in% FIELDS_IN_SCOPE),
  !any(grepl("Opisthokonta", paired$full_classification) &
         !grepl("Choanoflagell", paired$full_classification)),   # choanoflagellates only
  sum(units$vent_bin == "Vent") == 13, sum(units$vent_bin == "Non-vent") == 6,
  !anyDuplicated(ko_hab$ko_id), !anyDuplicated(tax_hab$cur_L4),
  # shares sum to 1 within each unit
  all(abs(summarise(group_unit, s = sum(share), .by = unit)$s - 1) < 1e-8),
  all(abs(summarise(tax_unit, s = sum(share), .by = unit)$s - 1) < 1e-8),
  # each class-level taxon sits in exactly one curated group
  !anyDuplicated(distinct(tax_unit, cur_group, cur_L4)$cur_L4),
  # vent-only = never detected in background water (plume allowed)
  all(ko_hab$n_det_background[ko_hab$habitat_class == "vent_only"] == 0),
  all(ko_hab$n_det_vent[ko_hab$habitat_class %in% c("vent_only", "vent_skewed", "shared")] >= MIN_UNITS[["vent"]]),
  all(abs(summarise(class_kegg, s = sum(pct_of_mapped), .by = habitat_class)$s - 100) < 1e-6)
)
```
